newsitem.title: USA: BMW introduces industry-first, head-and-neck airbag.
newsitem.headline: BMW introduces industry-first, head-and-neck airbag.

text.p: BMW of North America Inc. Wednesday became the latest company to upgrade its airbag system, announcing a new head-and-neck inflation device the German automaker said was the first of its kind in the world.

The new head protection system will begin showing up this June as a standard feature on 7 Series cars in the United States, said Henrich Heitmann, chief executive officer of BMW (US) Holding Corp., a unit of Bayerische Motoren-Werke AG.
Heitmann announced the new device at a breakfast meeting that kicked off the press days for the New York International Auto Show. The show opens to the public March 29.

By the end of this year, the head protection system will be available on all BMW sedans. Side impact airbags that do not protect the head and neck are already available on BMW's 3 Series sedans, and all 5 Series and 7 Series models.

Audi, a unit of Volkswagen AG, and Lexus, the luxury car division of Toyota Motor Corp., also will offer side airbags. Last year, Volvo and Mercedes-Benz, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG, were the only automakers to have the side impact devices.
Detroit's Big Three also have said they plan to introduce side impact airbags on future models, but so far none have been announced.
The BMW system, which will be on both sides of the car, is not expected to add significantly to the cost of the vehicle, BMW officials said.

The new head airbag is a long tube that is stored in the roof panel above each front door. Upon impact, it inflates and protects a passenger's head and neck from the windshield pillar, window and center pillar. The bag stays inflated for about five seconds after the initial impact to ward off further injury.
According to BMW, about 21 percent of all motor vehicle accidents are side impact collisions, accounting for 36 percent of all fatalities.

Airbags have been under scrutiny lately, following complaints from safety groups who want their deployment force reduced. Airbags have been blamed for the deaths of 38 children and 24 adults. The U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration recently changed its testing rules to allow automakers to install less explosive airbags later this year.
Also Wednesday, Heitmann said BMW will this year enter the heavyweight cruiser segment of the motorcyle industry with a new bike called the BMW Cruiser.
Annual worldwide sales volume for the Cruiser will be about 10,000 units. Only about 1,500 are expected to be available in the United States in 1997.
